title: Changing through fear: exploring fantasy and the potential of funas to prevent sexual aggression in flirting
abstract: This article examines how the threat of being called out – funao – shapes the sexual subjectivities and flirting practices of heterosexual teenage men in Chile. Focusing on the rise of feminist funas (online public denunciations of sexual or gender-based violence), it explores how fear of exposure functions as a paranoid fantasy that reconfigures men’s conduct even when they cannot articulate why certain behaviours are unacceptable. Drawing on psychosocial theories of fantasy, affect and masculinity, the article argues that funas act as affective pedagogies, disciplining young men’s behaviours and contributing ambivalently to the prevention of gender-based violence – not through explicit political conviction but through anticipation and shame. The analysis is based on online interviews with high-school students conducted during Chile’s 2019–2021 social uprising. Findings show how young men portray the funao as a passive victim, mobilise myths of miscommunication, and express both fear and confusion in response to feminist scrutiny. These accounts demonstrate how fantasy helps us grasp not only what participants say but also how they feel their way through a shifting sexual culture, where violence is imagined as a possibility that resides ‘between men’. The article contributes by demonstrating the value of fantasy as an analytic for studying sexual cultures, capturing the affective and anticipatory dimensions of change beyond cognitive or structural accounts. Situated in the Chilean context, the case also contributes to global discussions on digital feminist practices and men’s transformations, illustrating how feminist politics can simultaneously unsettle normative masculinity and generate ambivalent, uneven routes to change.
